title: Bass drum versus snare drum in parades; shrinking drum sizes
summary: Robertson explains the bass drum comes in only when the snare cues it, that the snare works harder, and that the 22-inch bass drum replaced bigger, punishing ones.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: I was going to ask about the bass drum. You know the bass drum doesn't play all the time on the street. The snare drum in between the pieces. Yes, snare drum kick has all the time. Was there ever a time when the bass drum would play with the snare drum?

No. Sometimes those fellas just do it, you know, say ordinary parades like that. The bass drum go along like that. But you don't have to. But that snare drum can't time all the time until it's time to play. Then the bass drum come in. But the bass drum, the fact of it, he don't work as hard as the snare drum. The snare drum don't never have no rhythm. He always works. The bass drum. If they walk two blocks, he can walk two blocks in the north. If they walk two blocks in the north. If they walk two blocks in the north. If they walk two blocks in the north. If they walk two blocks in the north. But that snare drum has got to still keep that time from the walk by.
Of course you have the job carrying that big bass drum. Yours isn't awfully big as how big is it. No, they all make them small now. Is that 22 inches or something?

Yeah, that's the 22. Now you see the children here, it's just a bigger drummer than that. See, they're getting away from that type of drummer. That drum was too big. It was too big. It was killing drummers.
Can you come around there, please?
